headline: Elevated, steady: Iran now says a supertanker carrying about 2 million barrels sank after a mine blast in Hormuz, so fuel stays the main risk for SA as oil markets reopen today.
summary: Iran says a supertanker carrying about 2 million barrels of oil sank in the Gulf after hitting a mine, on top of earlier claims of five tankers and a tug on fire; these are Iran's claims and are not independently confirmed. Oil markets reopen today, so watch for a Brent and bowser price jump; Australia remains at Level 2 of the National Fuel Security Plan. Last night's spike in Gulf GPS jamming (31%) has eased to 21% with no new strikes confirmed. Locally it is quiet: Moderate fire danger in the Hills, no fire bans or CFS warnings, and the grid and phone networks are normal.
actions: If you haven't topped up the car this weekend, do it early today before any oil price jump reaches SA bowsers.
Check your bushfire plan and CFS app watch zones now that the Fire Danger Season has started.

categories.name: Geopolitical & conflict
categories.summary: Iran says a supertanker with about 2 million barrels sank after a mine blast, after earlier claims of five tankers and a tug on fire; not independently confirmed. Gulf GPS jamming spiked to 31% overnight and has eased to 21%. Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no new warning signs; Latvia's mobilisation drill is a planned exercise.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal, no unusual private-jet movements, and forecast markets show no jump.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: All Australian carriers normal and the SA grid normal. Microsoft says its 365 service is restored. A French bank reportedly lost about EUR 100 million in a cyber attack likely aided by AI; global threat level is green. The ACSC alert feed timed out this run.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological
categories.summary: WHO reports the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continuing in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria and MERS cases in Qatar; no cases outside those regions. The 'chlorine poisoning' sign is a German hotel accident during the Microsoft outage, not an attack. Two of seven Adelaide emergency departments are very busy, below the warning threshold.

sources.title: WHO: Ebola (Bundibugyo) - DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: Fire danger Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges today and tomorrow, no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans, CFS warnings or severe-weather warnings. A structure fire at Geranium and a grass fire at Maitland are being handled; outback roads in the north-east remain closed by flooding.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply
categories.summary: Hormuz carries about 4 ships a day (100+ before the war) and Iran now claims a supertanker sank. Australia is at Level 2 of the National Fuel Security Plan; petrol is around 234 c/L and diesel near 278 c/L nationally. Malacca, Lombok, Sunda and Torres routes are normal.

sources.title: IBTimes: Australian petrol prices ease, diesel near 278c

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: Friday close: Brent US$95.84, VIX 19.3, gold US$3,886, AUD 0.678. The weekend's Hormuz reports came after the close, so oil and the dollar may move when markets reopen today.

Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi missiles; debris falls in Mecca region
Iran reports a strike on Sirik on its Hormuz coast

concerns.title: Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz shipping
drivers: Iran says a supertanker carrying about 2 million barrels of oil sank in the Gulf after a mine explosion, after earlier claims of five tankers and a tug on fire; these are Iran's claims and are not independently confirmed.
Hormuz carries about 4 ships a day; Gulf GPS jamming spiked to 31% overnight and has eased to 21%, with no new US strikes confirmed.
Forecast markets give about 15% for a US-Iran Hormuz deal by year end, down 4 points.

scenarios.name: Standoff drags on with mine and ship incidents
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices stay high and may jump this week; occasional regional servo shortages but no rationing.

scenarios.name: Deal reached, shipping recovers
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices ease over weeks; little direct effect on SA.

scenarios.name: Major escalation: renewed US/Israeli strike campaign or wider Gulf attacks
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel price jump and local shortages within 1-3 weeks; possible government fuel measures.

actions.action: Top up the car and any generator fuel early today.
actions.reason: Oil markets reopen today after a weekend of tanker reports; price rises reach SA bowsers within days.

actions.action: Hold a little cash at home.
actions.reason: If fuel is rationed or networks fail, cash still works when cards may not.

concerns.title: Cyber attacks and outages hitting Australian services
drivers: No Australian carrier outage and the SA grid is normal; the global threat level is green.
Microsoft 365 is restored and was not an attack; a Check Point firewall flaw is still being exploited.

scenarios.name: Ongoing breaches and occasional cloud outages
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of disruption to email and online services; scam risk from stolen data.

scenarios.name: Hours-long outage of payments or a telco
scenarios.sa_impact: Card payments and phones down for hours.

scenarios.name: Multi-day multi-sector attack
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, fuel and communications disrupted for days.

actions.action: Keep devices and banking apps updated.
actions.reason: Most attacks on households exploit known flaws that updates already fix.

concerns.title: AI-enabled attack (non-traditional)
drivers: A French bank reportedly lost about EUR 100 million in an attack likely aided by AI, and a report describes an AI-driven campaign against semiconductor and defence firms; none target Australia specifically.
No deepfakes of officials or fake alerts have been reported in Australia.

scenarios.name: Background AI-assisted crime and espionage
scenarios.sa_impact: More convincing scams and data breaches; no wide outage.

scenarios.name: Synthetic-media crisis (fake leader video or alert)
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of confusion, possible panic buying before it is debunked.

scenarios.name: Machine-speed attack on many systems at once
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, telcos, hospitals or the grid disrupted for hours to days.

actions.action: Agree a family code word for urgent calls.
actions.reason: AI can clone a voice from seconds of audio; a code word defeats fake 'I need help now' calls.

concerns.title: Local SA emergency (bushfire, heat, power) within 7 days
drivers: Fire danger is Moderate in the Hills and there is no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans, CFS warnings or severe-weather warnings.
The SA grid is normal; a structure fire at Geranium and a grass fire at Maitland are local incidents, and flood road closures are in the far north-east.

scenarios.name: Quiet week
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Hot, windy day with fire bans
scenarios.sa_impact: Fire danger High to Extreme in the Hills; travel plans may need changing.

scenarios.name: Damaging fire or major power outage
scenarios.sa_impact: Evacuations, power and phone outages in affected areas.

actions.action: Check your bushfire plan and the CFS app alert zones before the first hot spell.
actions.reason: Early-season fires start fast, and decisions are easier made on a calm day.

concerns.title: Taiwan Strait pressure
drivers: Taiwan reports Chinese 'area denial' drills in the Western Pacific; this is pressure, not a blockade.
No live-fire warnings, GPS jamming or internet disruption around Taiwan; strait shipping is normal and forecast markets give about 3% for a clash before 2027.

scenarios.name: Routine grey-zone pressure
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Large announced drill
scenarios.sa_impact: Market jitters; no supply effect.

scenarios.name: Blockade or quarantine
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel, medicine and electronics disruption within weeks.

actions.action: Keep 2-3 months of any essential prescription medicines.
actions.reason: Most medicines are imported via Asian shipping lanes, which any blockade would disrupt first.

concerns.title: Ebola in Africa and MERS in the Gulf
drivers: WHO reports the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continuing in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria with no cases outside Africa, and MERS cases in Qatar linked to camel contact.
Two of seven Adelaide emergency departments are very busy, below the level that would suggest an outbreak.

scenarios.name: Outbreaks stay contained in their regions
scenarios.sa_impact: No direct effect; possible extra airport screening.

scenarios.name: Isolated imported case in a Western country
scenarios.sa_impact: Media concern; Australian hospitals manage under existing plans.

scenarios.name: Spread in Asia-Pacific
scenarios.sa_impact: Travel restrictions and health system alerts.

actions.action: Check Smartraveller before any travel to Central or East Africa or the Gulf.
actions.reason: Advice and entry rules can change quickly as outbreaks and the conflict develop.

concerns.title: Undersea cables and Australian networks
drivers: No foreign vessels are on the cable watch list near Australia and all Australian carriers are normal.
No undersea cable damage reported near Australia.

scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.sa_impact: Slower international internet for days; traffic reroutes via other cables.

scenarios.sa_impact: Major internet, payments and cloud disruption across Australia.
